proposals.before: When Quyu died, his son Yiyi was established.
proposals.after: When Quyu died, his son Yiwu was established.
proposals.reason: Chinese 夷吾 is Yiwu; the idiomatic spelling Yiyi does not match the characters or the literal field.

proposals.before: When Yiyi died, his son Qinchu was established.
proposals.after: When Yiwu died, his son Qinchu was established.
proposals.reason: The same 夷吾 is again rendered Yiyi; keep Yiwu to match the Chinese name.

proposals.before: From Huo below, no criticism there.
proposals.after: From Kuai and below, there was no criticism.
proposals.reason: 鄶 is Kuai, not Huo; the literal line mistransliterates the state/air name already given as Kuai in the idiomatic field.

proposals.before: Saw dance elephant trunk, south flute, said: 'Beautiful indeed, still have emotion.'
proposals.after: Saw the Xiangshuo and Nanyue dances, said: 'Beautiful indeed, still have feeling.'
proposals.reason: 象箾 and 南籥 are Zhou court dances (xiang-flute and southern yue), not an elephant trunk and a south flute.

proposals.before: Saw dance Zhao trunk, said: 'Virtue utmost indeed, great indeed, like heaven no not cover also, like earth no not carry also, although very flourishing virtue, nothing add.
proposals.after: Saw the Zhaoshuo dance, said: 'Virtue has reached its utmost, great indeed, like heaven covering all, like earth carrying all; although very flourishing virtue, nothing to add.'
proposals.reason: 招箾 is a dance name (Zhaoshuo/Shaoshuo), not a Zhao trunk; the literal field corrupts the proper noun.

proposals.before: The ruler is extravagant and has many favorites, and the grandees are all rich. The government will end up in the hands of the three families.
proposals.after: The ruler is extravagant and has many good men, and the grandees are all rich. The government will end up in the hands of the three families.
proposals.reason: Chinese 多良 means many good or worthy men, not favorites (嬖).

proposals.before: He often thought: The four brothers of my father should have passed the throne to Jizi.
proposals.after: He often thought: My father and his brothers, four men, should have passed the throne to Jizi.
proposals.reason: 吾父兄弟四人 is the four brothers of that generation including Guang’s father, not four brothers of the father excluding him.

proposals.before: Wu Zixu's initial fled to Wu, persuaded Wu king Liao with attacked Chu benefits.
proposals.after: When Wu Zixu first fled to Wu, he persuaded King Liao of Wu of the benefits of attacking Chu.
proposals.reason: Literal English is ungrammatical ('initial fled') and omits finite verbs; the Chinese is a complete clause about Zixu's first flight and persuasion.

proposals.before: In the sixth year, Chu sent Zichang and Nang Wa to attack Wu.
proposals.after: In the sixth year, Chu sent Zichang Nang Wa to attack Wu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 子常囊瓦 names one Chu commander (courtesy name 子常 plus personal name 囊瓦), not two separate envoys.

proposals.before: Chu feared and left Ying moved to Rui.
proposals.after: Chu feared and left Ying, moved to Ruo.
proposals.reason: Literal English renders 鄀 as Rui; the toponym is Ruo (鄀), matching the idiomatic line.

proposals.before: King Helu’s younger brother Fu wanted to battle, but Helu would not permit it.
proposals.after: King Helu’s younger brother Fugai wanted to battle, but Helu would not permit it.
proposals.reason: The same man is 夫槩 at s0215; 夫 here is the shortened personal name Fugai, and keeping Fu only in this line obscures the identity later spelled Fugai.

proposals.before: Di Xiang consort Hou Zhen just pregnant, fled to You Ren and gave birth Shao Kang.
proposals.after: Di Xiang consort Hou Min just pregnant, fled to You Ren and gave birth Shao Kang.
proposals.reason: 后緡 is Hou Min/Houmin; the literal rendering Hou Zhen misreads 緡.

proposals.before: Wu king heard this, greatly angered, granted Zixu the Lou sword to die.
proposals.after: Wu king heard this, greatly angered, granted Zixu the Shulou sword to die.
proposals.reason: 屬鏤 is the sword-name Zhulou/Shulou; Lou sword drops 屬.

proposals.before: Wu people reported defeat to king Fu Chai, Fu Chai hated their hearing it.
proposals.after: Wu people reported the defeat to King Fuchai; Fuchai hated that the report was heard.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 惡其聞也 means he hated the news becoming known, not that he hated 'their hearing it'.

proposals.before: The king of Wu said: “I am old and lonely, and I can no longer serve the lord king.
proposals.after: The king of Wu said: “I am old, and I can no longer serve the lord king.
proposals.reason: 孤 is the royal first-person pronoun, not a claim that Fuchai is lonely; 孤老矣 means he is old.

proposals.before: Wu king said: 'I am orphaned and old, cannot serve lord king also.
proposals.after: Wu king said: 'I am old; I cannot serve the lord king.'
proposals.reason: 孤 is royal self-reference, not 'orphaned'; the literal English invents orphanhood.

decisions.reason: 夷吾 is Yiwu; Yiyi matches neither the characters nor the unit’s own literal rendering Yiwu.
The same 夷吾 is again spelled Yiyi; the successor sentence must use Yiwu.
鄶 is Kuai, the odes-state already so named in the idiomatic line; Huo is a different graph.

decisions.after: Saw dance Xiangshuo, Nanyue, said: 'Beautiful indeed, still have emotion.'
decisions.reason: 象箾 and 南籥 are dance names, not an elephant trunk and a south flute, but the proposal also idiomatizes a literal line and needlessly swaps emotion for feeling.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 見舞象箾、南籥者，曰：「美哉，猶有感。」

decisions.after: Saw dance Zhaoshuo, said: 'Virtue utmost indeed, great indeed, like heaven no not cover also, like earth no not carry also, although very flourishing virtue, nothing add.
decisions.reason: 招箾 is the dance Zhaoshuo, not a Zhao trunk; the rest of the calque already tracks 無不燾 / 無不載 and should not be rewritten as idiomatic English.
多良 is many worthy/good men; favorites would be 嬖, which the Chinese does not have.
吾父兄弟四人 is Guang’s father plus his brothers as a set of four, confirmed by the next unit that his father was established first; “four brothers of my father” wrongly excludes him.
The telegraphic calque already reports Zixu’s first flight to Wu and persuasion of King Liao about attacking Chu; the proposal only recasts the literal field as idiomatic English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 伍子胥之初奔吳，說吳王僚以伐楚之利

decisions.reason: 子常囊瓦 is one Chu commander, courtesy name 子常 plus personal name 囊瓦, not two men joined by and.
鄀 is Ruo; Rui transcribes a different place-name.
This unit writes only 夫; Fu is an accurate rendering of the graph present here, and expanding it to Fugai imports 槩 from a later sentence.
后緡 is Hou Min; Zhen is a misreading of 緡.

decisions.after: Wu king heard this, greatly angered, granted Zixu the Zhulou sword to die.
decisions.reason: 屬鏤 is the full sword name, so Lou is incomplete, but this chapter’s idiomatic line and claims already use Zhulou rather than Shulou.
惡其聞也 is calqued by “hated their hearing it” (hated that it was heard); the rewrite mainly polishes literal style without changing the supported sense.
孤 is the royal first person; 孤老矣 says he is old and does not claim loneliness.

decisions.after: Wu king said: 'I am old, cannot serve lord king also.
decisions.reason: 孤 is royal self-reference, so “orphaned” invents a biography, but the proposed line also drops the calque and over-smooths the rest of the literal field.

claimRevisions.reason: The English personal name Yiyi was produced only by the bad idiomatic spelling; 夷吾 is Yiwu.
